Foreword: I am using imgur for the sake of longevity. There is some minor conflicting information you may come across, for example his age. He is 38 as far as I have found, though some articles I have come across (not listed here) stated he was 31.

 

Kris Fowler, 38, hiking in Washington – good write up covering his case and provides many pictures: http://archive.is/UCO35

News Article One Month After Disappearance: http://archive.is/zsRLR

Kris started his hike in Campo, California with the intent to follow the Pacific Crest Trail all the way to the Canada border. http://i.imgur.com/vxMtTmw.png

 

He went to Packwood before hitching a ride back to White Pass, debating on continuing as the weather was supposed to get nasty. He tells an employee at Krackerbarrel in White Pass that he is continuing on to Snoqualmie Pass. http://i.imgur.com/odmD4Y6.png

 

October 10th in Packwood, Fowler was found squatting in a trailer wearing sandals and said he was cold: http://archive.is/l7HhU

 

His sandals. That is something that is pointed out in almost every single article I have come across. Not exactly the best foot wear for long-term hiking in PNW. There was this little blog that mentions he might have changed to trail runners at some point http://archive.is/wfAku (though the two thru hikers who spent some time with him nearer his disappearance always described him as wearing sandals).

 

He also tells employee that his phone was not charging properly, which addresses the lack of ping or attempts to contact after that. His cell phone “disappeared from satellite view” at 5:43 PM on October 12th and “has never returned”.

 

He is seen between White Pass and Snoqualmie (closer to the latter) by two bear hunters. They are the last to make contact with him. No one knows if he continued north to Canada, went off trail (as he sometimes did) or what. http://i.imgur.com/x2Y9hE1.png

He had a Spot GPS device and did not activate it. (from first article listed)

A youth hiker near the Washington border met Kris Fowler at a campsite where they hung out and chatted for awhile said that Fowler had,

a fierce determination to reach the finish in Canada.

He hiked with some other “thru” hikers for awhile, who were impressed by his skill and smarts (which got him the nickname 'Sherpa' among other hikers).

 

To note:

The next morning after a heavy snowfall, Murrow and Hampton found Fowler again under his stack of gear he used to keep warm during the night. This time, he decided to hike with them since they had GPS, preferable to his paper maps along the Goat Rocks, where sometimes steep embankments were covered with snow and thick fog.

The above gives some perspective into Kris Fowler's technique. To me, it goes to show how unlikely it is for Kris to willingly separate himself from his gear. Also, the lack of a GPS is important (he had a locating device, but that isn't the same thing).

Credit card charges also stopped after Oct. 12, when Fowler would have been the last known northbound thru hiker to start the relatively easy 29-mile section of trail from White Pass to Chinook Pass. But sheriff’s Sgt. Briscoe said another hiker who knew Fowler well from earlier in their journey took the trail south during the same time frame, and he saw no sign of Fowler.

An easy stretch of trail and Fowler was the only current check in to be heading north – as well as the last for the season. The only south bound hiker, who knew Fowler, saw no sign of him. Very curious.

Two hunters who exchanged small talk with Fowler on Oct. 22 at Blowout Mountain offered the most credible sighting, when they correctly described him to Briscoe in early November even before they saw a photo.

The above can be found in this article: http://archive.is/b1zIq  

More important points:

 

  • No bank use after October 12th (his last cell signal as picked up by satellite as well)

  • Step-Mother grows concerned, begins trying to find him October 19th.

  • She last received a text from him September 30th.

  • The family began to contact local authorities October 28th as well as head north to start their search which lasted 10 days.

  • Location he went missing (topographical and satellite): http://i.imgur.com/ja7c0U1.png

 

The sear for Fowler was fairly extensive and covered 100 miles of the Pacific Crest Trail in Washington. On top of local law enforcement, SAR and volunteers, 8 other Washington counties as well as the Air National guard joined the search. This resulted in many air search hours and a lot of boots on the ground.

 

At the writing of this article: http://archive.is/vnaAw on November 23rd, 2016, some searchers intended to keep an eye out for the man throughout the winter, already planning out snowmobile teams and search patterns.

 

March 14th, 2017 - Thus far, no sign of Fowler has been found. None of his gear, nothing. I haven't been able to find articles that go into all search patterns, including canines and reactions. Weather pattern seemed typical for that time of year, hard to predict but lots of rain and cold.
